headline: Where Moor Meets Sea: Essential Exmoor Visitor Guide
reservation: The park is free to enter, but car parks at popular sites like Valley of Rocks or Dunkery Beacon may require local fees. Stargazing events during the October Dark Skies Festival typically require advance booking. Accommodation in small hamlets like Simonsbath is limited and should be secured well in advance.

days.title: The Wilderness Coast

stops.name: Valley of Rocks
stops.detail: Walk among dramatic rock formations along the rugged heritage coastline.

stops.name: Great Hangman
stops.detail: Ascend England’s highest sea cliffs for views from 314 metres above the Bristol Channel.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for coastal road transit; conditions vary
days.note: Steep gradients are common near Lynton and Lynmouth; allow extra time for heavy vehicles.

days.title: High Moors and Rivers

stops.name: Dunkery Beacon
stops.detail: Visit the highest point on Exmoor and Somerset for panoramic views of the heather moors.

stops.name: Tarr Steps
stops.detail: Observe this ancient clapper bridge over the River Barle; check for current accessibility after storm events.

days.driving: Allow 1.5-2 hours for moorland driving; conditions vary
days.note: Roads across the high moor are often open and exposed; watch for wandering Exmoor ponies.

days.title: Villages and Ancient Vales

stops.name: Porlock Weir
stops.detail: Explore this historic harbor village situated at the edge of the Vale of Porlock.

stops.name: Selworthy Beacon
stops.detail: Look for heather in bloom and views across Porlock Bay from this high vantage point.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local valley transit; conditions vary
days.note: Porlock Hill features one of the steepest A-road gradients in the UK; check vehicle brakes.

intel.title: Permits and Village Lots
intel.text: Parking permits can be purchased in advance via the official shop for major National Park lots. Village parking in Dulverton or Porlock is available but limited during festival periods.

intel.title: Moorland Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular signal is highly inconsistent in deep wooded combes and the central moor near Simonsbath. Main villages usually provide basic coverage, but do not rely on it for emergency navigation.

intel.title: Perimeter Service
intel.text: The nearest mainline rail stations and major fuel hubs are in Taunton, Barnstaple, and Tiverton Parkway. Ensure a full tank before heading into the interior moorland roads.

intel.title: Wildlife Viewing
intel.text: Dawn and dusk are the best times to catch a glimpse of wild red deer stags at Alderman's Barrow. Stargazing is optimal on clear moonless nights in the Dark Sky Reserve.

intel.title: Coastal Path Routes
intel.text: Around 1,000km of rights of way are maintained. The South West Coast Path follows the 'Wilderness Coast' and requires sturdy footwear for steep-sided gorges.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Taunton or Tiverton Parkway stations, followed by a bus or rental car transfer. Stock up on local produce in Dulverton before heading to remote moorland stays.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for cars, but large RVs may struggle with steep coastal hills and narrow village lanes. Always check rental height restrictions for rural bridges.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from Selworthy Beacon offers views of Porlock Bay framed by heather, with colors varying by season.
